facts.heading: Anxiety worsening since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it has gotten worse since September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Became deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school. She has taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school. I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah thinks people might notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxious thoughts occur mostly on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing staff meeting questions
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say for the staff meeting.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask, and what I'd say. Then what they'd think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Imagines being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice Year 4 teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of seeming stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargreaves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargreaves' reaction
facts.content: Mr Hargreaves told Hannah he was delighted in September.
facts.evidence: He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling like a liar
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr Hargreaves about her capability.
facts.evidence: I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Pretending to be capable
facts.content: Hannah feels she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable. As if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing self to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to her mother's potential.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's past career
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy noted
facts.content: People in the village still mention Hannah's mother's wonderful headship.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement date
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago

facts.heading: Mother's library named
facts.content: A library in the village has been named after Hannah's mother.
facts.evidence: they've named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fuss
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss when her mother offers support.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel I'm making a fuss.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine, then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking due to tasks
facts.content: Hannah wakes up at four to manage various tasks.
facts.evidence: going through the to-do list. Everything. Timetable changes, the Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about.

facts.heading: Waking since term started
facts.content: Hannah has been waking up this way since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term.

facts.heading: Drinks many cups of coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences physical symptoms in the afternoons when she cannot sit still.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah hid her physical symptoms from others.
facts.evidence: I said I was fetching a document.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I'm exhausted by the end of every day just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice received
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben advised her to enjoy the situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty and alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and alone when her partner gives advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty, and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner's profession and view
facts.content: Ben is an engineer and believes problems can be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer, he thinks if something's a problem you fix it.

facts.heading: Difficulty with social contact
facts.content: Hannah has lost friends at school and feels awkward in her role as line manager.
facts.evidence: Not any more, not really. I used to eat lunch in the Year 4 corridor with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Misses the children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and the daily interactions with them.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Misses the children's experiences
facts.content: Hannah misses the feeling of children receiving something new.
facts.evidence: The children, honestly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Wanted the promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion and accepted it because she couldn't say no.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Tears about fear of return
facts.content: Hannah cried after accepting the promotion due to fear of never going back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I'd never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Difference during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, Hannah did not think about school.
facts.evidence: I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Pre-term distress
facts.content: Hannah was distressed the week before term started.
facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again.

facts.heading: Refusal to eat on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah was unable to eat on Sunday before term started.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A child laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks

facts.heading: Stopped writing down things
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing down good things because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: and then I stopped, because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging.

facts.heading: Goal to avoid feeling fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal for Tuesday at work
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing it first and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without her stomach in knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling lighter after sharing
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful after saying her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: First time telling someone
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad things are before.
facts.evidence: That it's the first time I've told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows about the four a.m.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah is scared to tell Ben how bad things are because he might be hurt.
facts.evidence: He'd probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah is considering telling Ben this week.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Helpful time to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah thinks a quiet moment on a Saturday morning over breakfast would help her tell Ben.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yes, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Plan to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for a week.
facts.evidence: I could. I'll put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Nearly cancelled session
facts.content: Hannah nearly cancelled the session this morning.
facts.evidence: Only that I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
